sourceReviews.supportingSummary: Implement level 1 cache documents DAB 2.0+, REST-only scope, global and entity opt-in, quoted JSON property names, an entity TTL, and L1 versus L1L2. The intended values in c match its example, but every offered configuration omits required JSON key quoting. The current product article, not the contradictory training GraphQL example, supplies the behavior evidence.

choiceReviews.rationale: An entity with enabled false does not opt into caching, irrespective of its TTL and level. Those intended settings would describe a deliberate cache bypass, a legitimate alternative when fresh uncached reads are wanted. However, this exact offered text also has unquoted JSON keys, including ttl-seconds. No literal valid DAB configuration context exists for it without changing authored syntax; intent alone cannot pass code review.

L1L2 selects in-memory and distributed tiers, rather than the required in-memory-only tier. With appropriate distributed-cache setup, those values could serve a different two-tier, thirty-second caching requirement. That is a settings-level alternative, not validation of this literal text: unquoted cache, enabled, ttl-seconds and level are not JSON property names. There is no unchanged, executable DAB configuration context for this malformed fragment.

The intended values independently match the article: entity enablement true, TTL thirty seconds and level L1, with global caching already enabled. Nevertheless, the question offers this as a configuration, not explicitly as pseudocode. Even enclosed in an entity object it fails JSON parsing because keys are unquoted. It has no literal valid configuration context until rewritten with JSON quoting; that repair requires fresh passes.

A TTL of 120 seconds is not the requested thirty seconds, although enablement and the L1 tier are the intended kinds of settings. Those values suit an entity deliberately configured for a two-minute lifetime. As authored, however, the unquoted property names make the entire alternative invalid JSON. The positive settings context cannot supply a literal valid DAB fragment without an actual syntax repair.

review.verificationNotes: Reject the exact configuration alternatives, not the documented cache semantics. Each uses unquoted JSON property names; wrapping each fragment in an entity object still produced an actual JSON.parse SyntaxError. The intended c values match the current REST-only DAB 2.0 article, but silently quoting keys would repair authored content and invalidate this pass. No SQL or DAB execution occurred. Source allowlisting and the credential/path/module/entity-unit chain passed independently; the parent's conflicting GraphQL cache example was excluded. Comparison against 584 bank records and cohort metadata found no duplicate; full dp800-direct-019/020 and sibling 057 test distinct facts. Reauthor valid JSON before restarting the three-pass workflow.
review.confidenceReason: High confidence that the intended c settings are documented and that every literal offered fragment is invalid JSON. Approval cannot depend on an undeclared pseudocode interpretation or an unrecorded syntax repair.
